tasks.title: Create registry loader module
tasks.description: Build the registry runtime. Create apps/scene-engine/src/renderer/asset-registry.js exporting two functions: (1) loadRegistry(url = '/assets/registry.json') — async; fetches the JSON, stores it in a module-scoped Map, returns the parsed object; if already loaded for this url, returns the cached value without re-fetching. (2) resolveAsset(id) — sync; returns the registry entry { type, path } for the id, or null and emits console.warn(`[asset-registry] Unknown asset id: ${id}`). The module also exports getRegistry() for any consumer that needs the raw catalogue (e.g. CP4's asset browser). No side-effect imports; the consumer (scene-renderer in task 4) is responsible for awaiting loadRegistry before calling resolveAsset. Behavior on missing registry.json: log error, leave cache empty so resolveAsset returns null for everything (the renderer will then warn-and-skip per layer rather than failing the whole scene).

Add markDirty(): if (!store.dirty) { store.dirty = true; bus.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('dirty-changed', { detail: true })); }. Add markClean(): if (store.dirty) { store.dirty = false; bus.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('dirty-changed', { detail: false })); }. Add getDirty(): return store.dirty. (2) Add helper splitPath(path): returns ['0','children','2'] style array; if path is '' return []. The dot/'.children.' encoding stays the same as editor/src/path.js — split('.children.') and re-join with .children. between segments. (3) Add helper cloneAlongPath(scene, segments): produces a new scene where every layer object on the path is shallow-copied (so the leaf can be mutated without touching siblings). Returns { scene: clonedScene, parent, indexInParent, layer } where parent is the array containing the leaf (top-level scene.layers or some children[]) and indexInParent is the leaf's index in that array. Implementation: recursively descend; at each level shallow-copy the array containing the next segment and the layer at that segment. (4) Add mutateLayerAt(path, patch): const segs = splitPath(path); if (segs.length === 0) return; const { scene, parent, indexInParent, layer } = cloneAlongPath(store.scene, segs); const merged = mergePatch(layer, patch); parent[indexInParent] = merged; store.scene = scene; markDirty(); bus.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('scene-changed', { detail: scene })). (5) Add helper mergePatch(target, patch): produces a new object with patch applied — for each key in patch, if patch[key] is a plain object AND target[key] is a plain object, recurse; otherwise patch[key] wins. Plain-object check: typeof === 'object' && !Array.isArray && constructor === Object. (6) Add addLayerAt(parentPath, index, layer): parentPath '' means top-level. Resolve parent via splitPath + cloneAlongPath (treating parentPath as a layer path that itself gets cloned + has its children array copied) — for parentPath '' the parent is scene.layers (clone scene + scene.layers). Splice layer in at index (clamped to [0, parent.length]). store.scene = newScene; markDirty(); dispatch 'scene-changed'. (7) Add removeLayerAt(path): splitPath; clone along path; parent.splice(indexInParent, 1); store.scene = newScene; clear selectedPath if it was equal-or-prefixed by the removed path; markDirty; dispatch. (8) Add moveLayer(fromPath, toPath): atomic — clone full scene once, perform an internal remove-by-path then insert-at-path on that single clone, then store.scene = newClone + single 'scene-changed' dispatch + markDirty. toPath is the target index path *as if the remove had not happened* — adjust the destination index by -1 if both paths share the same parent and toPath's last segment > fromPath's last segment (classic reorder index correction). For cross-parent moves no adjustment. (9) EXPORT mutateLayerAt, addLayerAt, removeLayerAt, moveLayer, markDirty, markClean, getDirty as named exports. Note: every mutator dispatches a single 'scene-changed' so canvas re-renders happen exactly once per logical edit. The dirty flag is set inside each mutator — callers don't need to also call markDirty.
